newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: S&P assigns A-plus rating to NZ's Kiwi Co-op dairy.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns A-plus rating to NZ's Kiwi Co-op dairy.

text.p: Credit rating agency Standard and Poor's said on Friday it had assigned its A-plus corporate credit rating to Kiwi Co-operative Dairies Ltd.
The ratings outlook for the company was stable, S&P said.

"Kiwi's rating reflects the company's position as one of the most efficient dairy manufacturing companies in the world, the effective subordination of supplier payments, the structure of the New Zealand dairy industry, and its importance to the country's export economy," S&P said.
But it said business risk was heightened by Kiwi's dependence on its main manufacturing site at Hawera, where 90 percent of production is based.
Kiwi had a strong competitive position, accounting for 26 percent of national milk intake, and the co-operative structure allowed it flexibility in determining its cost base.
Debt levels were expected to rise in the near term, peaking at about NZ$650 million in fiscal 1998.
The recent merger with Tui Milk Products Ltd would see total assets reach NZ$1.2 billion in fiscal 1998. Targeted equity-to-assets was about 40 percent.
Kiwi's low cost strucuture and strengthened position in both domestic and export markets should enable the company to maintain its conservative financial positon, S&P said.
